intro.title: Request Deduplication
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Angular application that demonstrates request deduplication. You will create a service that prevents duplicate HTTP requests from being sent simultaneously, improving performance and reducing server load. The core programming concept used is caching and tracking pending requests using a Map. You will work with Angular's HttpClient, RxJS Observables, and TypeScript to implement this pattern in a beginner-friendly way.
intro.usecase: Request deduplication is essential in Angular applications where multiple components might trigger the same API call simultaneously, such as in dashboard widgets displaying overlapping data or product filtering interfaces with interdependent controls. For example, in an e-commerce dashboard, clicking multiple category filters in quick succession could trigger duplicate requests for product listings, wasting bandwidth and potentially causing race conditions. Similarly, in financial applications with real-time stock tickers, multiple components watching the same symbol would benefit from sharing a single network request rather than making redundant calls. This pattern improves performance by preventing unnecessary network traffic and ensures data consistency across your application.
